verdict.rationale: Spline documents direct design-to-code export: scenes export as Vanilla JS, Three.js, React, Next.js and react-three-fiber code, or as a self-contained self-hosted ZIP that includes the Spline runtime, plus a `<spline-viewer>` web component and a Code API for driving scenes from existing code. That is shippable output, but the evidence shows exports that embed a scene and runtime rather than idiomatic, editable component code. No mapping from Spline components to codebase components is documented. missing for 10: component-to-code mappings between design components and production code components, evidence that exported code is editable or idiomatic rather than a runtime-wrapped scene, independent or hands-on corroboration of shipping exported code.

support.subject: As a developer, designs map to production code — component-to-code mappings or direct design-to-code output I can actually ship

citations.quote: Spline allows you to export the code of your scene as: Vanilla JS, Three.js, React, Next.js, react-three-fiber
The Self-Hosted export option in Spline allows you to export your entire project, including all assets and the Spline runtime, as a fully self-contained ZIP file.
`<spline-viewer>` is a native HTML web component and can be used with most web builders, frameworks, or browsers.
It enables you to trigger actions, modify object properties, and create dynamic, responsive 3D environments directly from your existing code and user interface.
